title.narrative: Child-centered needs assessments were expanded to;4 aditional municipal social programmes, for a total of 14 out of 64 (22%);municipalities implementing, contributing to reducing disparities and enhancing access to social services.;Over 500 municipal workers in 14 municipalities received training on needs-based programming, budgeting, and data-driven decision-making.

Level of child responsiveness of urban policies, spatial-planning standards and programmes that address the unique structural barriers to child well-being in urban settings, with a special focus on those living in slums and informal settlements

baseline.value: 16% coverage by child benefits (TSA) 25.5% children in absolute poverty

title.narrative: Extent to which national and local governance capacities for reducing child poverty at local level, have been enhanced with UNICEF support, including in humanitarian settings

title.narrative: Evidence generated on budgets and their linkages to child outcomes to improve budget allocations/expenditure for children, Text

baseline.value: No analysis of government expenditure for children or child-friendly budgeting

target.value: 2025:State structures at local and central level have capacity to apply child-friendly budgeting

actual.value: 2024:Currently, no central government agency in Georgia has the capacity to fully implement child-friendly budgeting practices.

title.narrative: Municipalities have integrated information management systems for social programming, Text

baseline.value: No municipalities have integrated IMS for social programming

target.value: 2023:Concept on the functionality of IMS on social programming is developed, costed and approved by respective authorities

actual.value: 2023:An information management system (MSDA) was developed and in the process of operationalization.
